calls.title: ABSURIA — International Abstract & Surrealist Photography Contest 2026
calls.description: First edition of a new international festival dedicated exclusively to abstract and surrealist photography. Open to amateur and professional photographers worldwide. 100 photographs selected for physical exhibition across multiple venues in Tours, Loire Valley, France from May to September 2026. Fourteen winners honoured at an awards ceremony in Tours in early May. Categories: Abstract Photography and Surrealist Photography, each with Professional and Amateur divisions plus a Young Hopefuls award. Winners receive the ABSURIA Trophy — a physical gold statuette created specifically for the contest. All nominees exhibited in 3D online galleries on the festival website. Printing costs covered by organisers. AI-generated images not accepted. Fee varies by number of works submitted: amateur €20–€40, professional €25–€50, up to 6 images per registration.
calls.summary: First international festival for abstract & surrealist photography. Physical exhibition in Tours, France. Trophy + online 3D gallery.

calls.title: Athens Photo Festival Dummy Award 2026
calls.description: International photobook dummy competition run by the Hellenic Centre of Photography as part of Athens Photo Festival. Open to all photographers and artists who use photography, regardless of age or nationality. Winner receives a publishing contract with Chose Commune for the production of a photobook with a production budget of up to €15,000 and a minimum print run of 400 copies. Winning project included in the festival's main exhibition programme at Benaki Museum in Athens. Twenty shortlisted dummies exhibited at the festival, ten included in the printed catalogue. Submit digitally via online form (PDF, max 10 MB) and mail one physical dummy copy postmarked by the deadline. Projects should be finalized upon submission. If already printed, editions must be under 100 copies. Fee €25 per project, €15 for additional projects by the same applicant.
jury: Cécile Sayuri Poimboeuf-Koizumi, Publisher, Chose Commune
Marta Weiss, Curator of Photography, Victoria and Albert Museum
Sylvia Sachini, Curator, APhF Book Program
calls.summary: Dummy award with Chose Commune publishing contract (up to €15K). 20 shortlisted exhibited at Athens Photo Festival, Benaki Museum.

calls.title: Motion
calls.description: Curated international group photography exhibition exploring motion in still images. Photography cannot create the illusion of motion the way moving images can, yet photographers have developed powerful techniques for capturing and evoking it — from long exposures and motion blur to freezing split-second moments of action. PH21 Gallery invites submissions for a themed group show at their venue in Barcelona's historic Gothic Quarter. One curator's choice and up to three honourable mentions will be announced. Curator's choice receives free entry (up to 15 images) for the next PH21 exhibition. Early bird deadline April 20 at reduced rates; final deadline April 27. Special rate for students and unwaged (€15–€20). All photographers 18+ worldwide may enter with original work. Images submitted by email as JPEG, longest side max 1200px. Exhibition June 27 – July 21, 2026.
jury: Zsolt Bátori, Photographer & Philosophy of Art
Borbála Jász, Art Historian & Philosophy of Art
calls.summary: Curated group show on motion in photography. Physical exhibition in Barcelona's Gothic Quarter. Student rates available.

calls.title: Manipulation & Illusion
calls.description: Open call exploring the terrain between what is seen and what is constructed. Seeking work that engages with manipulation and illusion as they relate to perception, belief, identity, and power. Themes include optical, sensory, and spatial illusion; distortion, misdirection, and scale; unreliable memory; propaganda and political persuasion; digital manipulation and curated environments; institutional narratives and manufactured truth; manipulation as artistic method; and altered materials, images, and data. All disciplines welcome — photography, visual art, design, and fine craft. Submissions accepted exclusively through the Co-Ex Collaborative website portal. Selected work featured in a curated online collection. Open worldwide.
calls.summary: Explore perception, belief, identity, and power through illusion and manipulation. All disciplines. Free, open worldwide.

calls.title: Epson International Pano Awards 2026
calls.description: 17th edition of the world's largest international competition for panoramic photography. Three main categories: Open (professional and amateur, $22/image), Amateur (non-professional photographers earning less than $20,000 from photography, $20/image), and VR/360 ($20/image) — plus a new Aerial category for drone and aircraft images. Total prize pool over US$50,000 including $15,000 in cash prizes. Open category winner receives a package exceeding $11,000. Early-bird entries close June 22 at standard rates; late entries accepted through July 13 at higher rates. Photographers who enter during the early-bird period are eligible for the $1,000 Curator's Award. Images must be panoramic format with aspect ratio greater than 2:1 (or less than 1:2 for verticals). All photographic capture methods welcome including digital, film, and stitched panoramas. Open worldwide.
calls.summary: World's largest panoramic photography competition. $50K+ prizes incl. $15K cash. New Aerial category. Open, Amateur, VR/360.

calls.title: REMEDY Photo Festival — Open Call 2026
calls.description: Photography festival focused on health, care, lived experience, and representation. Seeking photographic work exploring health in its broadest sense — physical, mental, chronic, invisible, communal, or systemic. Welcomes personal stories, portraiture, documentary, photojournalism, and fine art photography. Particularly interested in work by photographers with lived experience of long-term health conditions. Selected artists included in curated group exhibition at a photography gallery in Lincoln, with additional venues across Lincolnshire. No entry fee and no cost to exhibit — printing and display costs covered by the festival. Exhibition June 1–30, 2026. Past featured photographers include Anthony Luvera and JA Mortram.
calls.summary: Free festival exploring health — physical, mental, chronic, invisible. Lincoln, UK. Print and display costs covered.

calls.title: SQUARE Photography Exhibit
calls.description: Challenging photographers to compose within the square format — the most iconic and persistent format in photography. All photographic genres welcome including portraiture, landscape, documentary, architecture, and conceptual work. Twelve images selected for three-month exhibition at Decode Gallery in Tucson. Selected artists receive complimentary professional printing on Epson printers with Ilford Pearl paper, museum-quality 14×14 framing, and custom matting. Open worldwide to all skill levels. Exhibition August 1 – October 31, 2026.
calls.summary: Square format photography — all genres. Pro printing and museum framing included. Three-month exhibition in Tucson, AZ.

calls.title: Cumberland Valley Photographers 2026
calls.org: Washington County Museum of Fine Arts
calls.description: Annual juried photography exhibition at the Washington County Museum of Fine Arts, this year celebrating contemporary perspectives as the nation approaches its 250th anniversary. Photographers explore history, identity, place, and civic life through four themes: Unfinished Revolutions, Power of Place, Tell Everyone's Story, and American Experiment. Respond literally or metaphorically through documentary, conceptual, figurative, or abstract approaches. All photographic processes accepted. Submissions open April 1–30, 2026. Selected work exhibited June 20 – October 11, 2026. Open to photographers from Maryland, Virginia, West Virginia, Pennsylvania, and Washington, DC.
calls.summary: Juried museum exhibition on America's 250th anniversary themes. Open to MD, VA, WV, PA, DC photographers. All processes.

calls.title: UNSTAGED Journal — Issue 02: Eerie
calls.description: Second issue of UNSTAGED, an independent photography journal dedicated to lens-based inquiries into comforting and discomforting authenticity. Issue 02, guest curated by Karla Guerrero (Mexico City-based photographer, curator, and editor active in the contemporary photography scene), explores the theme Eerie — quiet disturbance, a poetics of phantasmagoria where images silently evoke meaning. The eerie as the fleeting suggestion that something unnameable lingers just beneath what we think we see. Something quietly disturbing. Submit 5–10 photographs as JPG files (long edge 2000px) with artist statement and bio. Upload work to Google Drive and send the link to reach@arek-ratai.com. Name files: Name_Series_Title_01. Free entry, free print publication for selected photographers.
calls.summary: Free indie photography journal on authenticity. Theme: Eerie. Guest curated by Karla Guerrero. Print publication.

calls.title: Canon Female Photojournalist Grant 2026
calls.description: 26th edition of the grant awarded in partnership with Canon, supporting female photojournalists pursuing long-term documentary projects. Winner receives €8,000 to support completion of an existing project or facilitate the making of a new one. Winning project exhibited at the Visa pour l'Image festival in Perpignan, France, September 2026. Open to professional female photojournalists worldwide, no age or nationality restrictions. Free entry. Winner selected in June by a jury of industry experts. Application window: March 18 – May 19, 2026.
calls.summary: €8,000 grant for female photojournalists. 26th edition with Canon. Long-term documentary projects. Exhibited at Perpignan.

calls.title: A Black Perspective: Celebrating the Voice & Vision
calls.description: Exhibition celebrating diverse narratives by Black photographers exploring resilience, heritage, joy, identity, and extraordinary aspects of Black life. Various photographic styles welcome including alternative practices and collage work. Juried by Arnika Dawkins, fine art photographer and founder of the Arnika Dawkins Gallery in Atlanta, specializing in imagery by and of African Americans. Selected work exhibited May 21 – June 19, 2026 at PhotoSC gallery, 918 Lady Street, Columbia, SC. Work must be printed 8x10" to 16x20", framed, and ready to hang.
jury: Arnika Dawkins, Fine Art Photographer & Gallery Founder
calls.summary: For Black photographers exploring resilience, heritage, joy, and identity. Exhibition in Columbia, SC. Juried by Arnika Dawkins.

calls.title: ANIMAL LIFE
calls.description: International juried photography exhibition celebrating the complexity and individuality of animals. Photographers invited to explore animal subjects with curiosity, empathy, and imagination — companion animals, wildlife, insects, and sea life through observation, environmental portraiture, documentary, or experimental approaches. Welcomes diverse perspectives on human-animal relationships. All lens-based photographic and lens-based art practices welcome, including black and white, color, traditional and non-traditional processes. Images showcasing violence or inhumane treatment will not be considered.
calls.summary: Exploring animal subjects with curiosity, empathy, and imagination. All lens-based work welcome. Minneapolis.

calls.title: FFSP 2026 — Italian Photographers Open Call
calls.org: Italian Cultural Institute of São Paulo
calls.description: Open call for Italian photographers as part of the São Paulo Photography Festival 2026, organized by the Italian Cultural Institute of São Paulo. Fifteen photographers will be selected for a free exhibition in May 2026 as part of the festival's official programme. One finalist will receive a round-trip flight between Brazil and Italy and official participation in FFSP 2026, fostering cultural and professional exchange between the two countries. Open to Italian citizens of legal age residing in Brazil or Italy. Submit 1 to 5 photographs on any theme of your choice.
calls.summary: Free exhibition in São Paulo for Italian photographers in Brazil/Italy. Winner receives round-trip airfare.

calls.title: Delfina Foundation — Latin America & Caribbean Residency 2026
calls.description: Twelve-week fully funded residency at the Delfina Foundation in London, supported by Jorge M. Pérez and El Espacio 23. Open to visual artists based in Latin America, the Caribbean, and related diasporic communities in the United States. Artists from Chile, Peru, Ecuador, Brazil, and Argentina are not eligible for this cycle (these countries received dedicated residencies in prior years). Two artists will be selected from this call: one for the autumn 2026 residency (September 21 – December 13) and one for the winter 2027 residency (January 5 – March 25). Apply via Cognito Forms with completed application form — read the Guidance Notes document before applying.
calls.summary: Fully funded 12-week residency in London for Latin American/Caribbean artists. Excludes Chile, Peru, Ecuador, Brazil, Argentina.

calls.title: MACK — Debut Photography Book Submissions
calls.description: MACK's annual submission window for first-time photobook authors. Founded by Michael Mack (former Managing Director of Steidl) in 2010, MACK is one of the most prestigious art and photography publishers in the world, releasing approximately 40 books per year with artists including Robert Adams, Alec Soth, and Wolfgang Tillmans. This window is specifically for artists who have not previously had a book published — seeking emerging voices and experimental approaches to the book form. Submit a PDF draft sequence and completed submissions form via email during the May 1–31 window only. No WeTransfer, Dropbox, or download links accepted. Email subject line: 'Submission: Debut Photography Book'. Response within one month after the window closes.
calls.summary: MACK's window for first-time photobook authors. One of the world's most prestigious photography publishers.

calls.title: MACK — Photography Submissions
calls.description: MACK's annual photography submission window. One of the world's most prestigious art and photography publishers, founded by Michael Mack in 2010 and based in London. This window seeks photobook projects that expand visual vocabulary and challenge expectations of photography's potential, with a special interest in voices and perspectives that are often underrepresented in the photobook landscape. Submit a PDF draft sequence and completed submissions form via email during the June 1–30 window only. No WeTransfer, Dropbox, or download links accepted. Email subject line: 'Submission: Photography'. Response within one month after the window closes.
calls.summary: MACK's annual photography window. Prioritizes underrepresented voices in the photobook landscape.

calls.title: Graz Residency for International Photographers (GRIP) 2026
calls.description: One-month residency for early-career photographers and lens-based artists in Graz, Austria. Fifth edition of GRIP, a joint initiative by Camera Austria and Kulturvermittlung Steiermark. Resident works on an ongoing project or develops new work, with access to Camera Austria's 11,000+ volume study library. Residency concludes with a presentation in Camera Austria's exhibition and library space. Open to international early-career artists working with photography and/or lens-based arts. Apply by email with informal statement of purpose and PDF portfolio.
calls.summary: One-month residency in Graz for early-career photographers. €1,000 stipend.

calls.title: Hidden Narratives Residency 2026
calls.description: Year-long residency engaging with the Royal Geographical Society's historic photographic collection of over one million pieces spanning 1845–1945. Artists explore materials relating to environment and humanitarian themes, developing work examining hidden narratives, loss, and human impact. Includes three research and presentation visits to the UK, a talk at Summit Photo 2026 (July 17–19), and an exhibition at Summit Photo 2027. In partnership with the Royal Geographical Society and the Italian Cultural Institute in London. Open to Italian visual artists, photographers, or practitioners with archive research experience, aged 18+, proficient in English.
jury: Danit Ariel, Artist, Writer & Photoworks Curator
Maria Teresa De Palma, Cultural Attaché, Italian Cultural Institute London
Jamie Owen, Curator, Royal Geographical Society
Rocco Venezia, Artist, Curator and Educator
calls.summary: Year-long residency with Royal Geographical Society's 1M+ photo archive (1845–1945). Three UK visits, Summit Photo exhibition. Italian artists only.

calls.title: Marilyn Stafford FotoReportage Award 2026
calls.description: Annual £4,000 grant for professional female photographers working on documentary photo essays that address social, environmental, economic, or cultural issues. Landmark 10th edition, supported by Nikon. Selected work must showcase positive solutions and demonstrate practical engagement with the subject matter. Named after Marilyn Stafford, pioneering documentary photographer. Winner's work exhibited at POST, Brighton & Hove's centre for photography, September 17–20, 2026, and featured on Lenscratch and FotoDocument. Open to female photographers (or those identifying as female) aged 18+ at any career stage, any nationality worldwide. Must have completed at least one prior documentary photo essay and already started the proposed project.
jury: Andrea Bruce, Photojournalist, NOOR Photo Agency co-owner, Nikon Ambassador
Donna De Cesare, Photojournalist, Associate Professor, University of Texas at Austin
Nina Emett, Director of FotoDocument, Documentary Photographer, Curator
Neo Ntsoma, Photojournalist, Founder of Neo Ntsoma Productions
Isabella Franceschini, 2024 Marilyn Stafford FotoReportage Award winner
calls.summary: £4,000 grant for female documentary photographers. 10th edition, supported by Nikon. Free entry. Exhibition at POST Brighton.

calls.title: Inge Morath Award 2026
calls.description: Annual award supporting women and nonbinary photographers under 30 working on long-term documentary projects. Administered by the Magnum Foundation in cooperation with Magnum Photos and the Inge Morath Estate. The recipient receives $7,500 and one finalist receives $1,000 to support completion of their project. Selected by the full membership of Magnum Photos during their Annual General Meeting, alongside the Inge Morath Estate and the Executive Director of the Magnum Foundation. Named after Austrian-born Magnum photographer Inge Morath (1923–2002). Now in its 25th year.
calls.summary: $7,500 grant for women/nonbinary photographers under 30. Long-term documentary project. 25th year. Selected by Magnum Photos membership.

calls.title: Women in Nature — Artist's Commission
calls.description: Photographic commission by Tóchar Midlands Wetland Restoration and Photo Museum Ireland highlighting the work of women in nature restoration in Ireland. €15,000 commission (including €3,000 travel bursary) for a single artist to create a series of 12 portraits of women in nature, together with photographs of the habitat they are working to restore. Outputs include exhibitions, community conversations, and a publication. Open to artists resident on the island of Ireland working in photography or lens-based media. Judged on creativity and originality (25%), technical skill and execution (20%), impact and storytelling (15%), and track record (10%). Co-financed by the EU Just Transition Fund and the Government of Ireland.
calls.summary: €15,000 commission for 12 portraits of women in nature restoration across Ireland. Exhibition + publication.

calls.title: Home
calls.description: Global open call exploring the theme of home — safety, belonging, dignity, identity, and place. In partnership with Fotografiska Emerging and the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights. Selected works will be exhibited at the United Nations Headquarters in New York on Human Rights Day, December 10, 2026. Curated by James Nachtwey and Pauline Benthede (Fotografiska Global VP Artistic Direction). Open to emerging photographers worldwide. 31 artists selected: 1 main image, 10 runner-ups, 20 honorable mentions. All forms of lens-based photography welcome, analog or digital. AI-generated or prompt-based images not accepted.
jury: Pauline Benthede, Global VP Artistic Direction, Fotografiska
Sophia Emmerich, Lead Editor, Fotografiska Emerging Platform
calls.summary: Exploring home — safety, belonging, dignity. Selected works exhibited at the United Nations HQ in New York.

calls.title: Exibart Street Photography Contest — 5th Edition
calls.description: Fifth edition of the international street photography contest by Exibart Street, Italy's leading contemporary art magazine. Two categories: Best Single Photo (€10) and Best Series of 3–9 images (€49). Winners receive a Leica Q3 or Xiaomi 17 Ultra with Leica lenses, plus interviews and editorial coverage across the Exibart network. Sponsored by Leica Camera. Open to photographers worldwide.
jury: Alan Schaller, Photographer, Co-founder Street Photography International (President)
Biba Giacchetti, Curator & Communication Strategist, Founder Sudest57 & Orion57
Andrea Pacella, Director Global Marketing & Communication, Leica Camera AG
Eolo Perfido, Creative Director & Leica Akademie Instructor, Editorial Director Exibart Street
Barbara Di Maio, Photographer & Researcher, Co-founder Women in Street Italy
Francesca Tiboni, Photographer, Co-founder Women in Street Italy
calls.summary: International street contest by Italy's leading art magazine. Leica Q3 grand prize. Five categories.

calls.title: RESTART2026
calls.description: International photography competition and exhibition for photographers starting their careers or reconsidering their creative direction with new work. Submit a series of 10–20 photographs created after 2021 that has not been fully exhibited or published. 10 finalists exhibit at Prospekto gallery in Vilnius. Top 3 winners receive individual exhibitions at Vilnius Photography Gallery the following year with partial production support. Printed catalogue for finalists. Featured on photography.lt and screened at NIDA Meeting Photography symposium in September.
jury: Gytis Skudžinskas, Artist, Book Artist & Curator
calls.summary: For photographers starting careers or reconsidering direction. 10-20 new photographs. Top 3 win solo exhibition in Vilnius.

calls.title: DPPF 2026 Sports Photography Grants
calls.description: Grants supporting emerging and early-career sports photographers with fewer than 3 years cumulative paid professional sports photography experience. Seven photographers receive $5,000 each for career development plus expenses-paid trip to the Sports Photography Gathering (September 16–18, 2026). Up to 3 winners eligible for year-long mentorship with Advisory Board members. Up to 3 additional applicants receive $2,500 Development Grants. Open worldwide except countries under active US sanctions.
calls.summary: Seven $5,000 grants for emerging sports photographers plus mentorship. Up to 3 additional $2,500 grants.

calls.title: Bowness Photography Prize 2026
calls.description: Australia's richest photography prize, now in its 20th year. Open to Australian citizens or permanent residents (12+ months). Winner receives $50,000 AUD and acquisition into MAPh's permanent collection. Two Honourable Mentions receive $2,500 each. Wai Tang Commissioning Award of $10,000 for a future exhibition. People's Choice Award of $5,000. Finalists exhibited at MAPh gallery. Accepts still photo-based media including analogue and digital photography produced within the past year. Up to 3 works per $55 entry. AI permitted only if not the substantial or overriding input. Entries open April 16, 2026.
calls.ai: Permitted if not the substantial or overriding input
calls.summary: Australia's richest photography prize. $50,000 AUD winner. 20th year. Australian citizens/residents only.

calls.title: Flanelle Print No. 47 — July 2026
calls.description: Montreal-based fashion and arts magazine (est. 2012) accepting submissions for Print No. 47, publishing July 2026. Open to artists, photographers, and designers worldwide. Selected work featured in quarterly print and digital magazine with international distribution. Two-phase review process. Work must be unpublished and exclusive to Flanelle. Paid upgrade options available for cover placement and priority publishing.
calls.summary: Montreal fashion and arts magazine. Quarterly print and digital with international distribution. Est. 2012.

calls.title: Embracing Our Differences 2027 Outdoor Exhibition
calls.description: International outdoor juried exhibition in its 23rd year. 50 selected artworks are displayed as billboard-sized panels (16 ft × 12.5 ft) in public parks in Sarasota and St. Petersburg, Florida, from January to April 2027. Three awards: $2,000 Best-in-Show Adult, $2,000 Best-in-Show Student, $2,000 People's Choice. Work must reflect themes of diversity, inclusion, kindness, and respect. Accepts photography, painting, drawing, mixed media, digital art. Horizontal orientation only. No limit on entries per artist. 150-word artist statement required. Over 5.2 million visitors since 2004. AI-generated work not accepted.
calls.summary: 50 artworks displayed as billboard-sized panels in Florida parks. Themes: diversity, inclusion, kindness.

calls.title: Night Aesthetics
calls.description: Open call exploring the visual world of the night. Looking for works that engage with light, movement, atmosphere, intimacy, and the energy that appears when the day lets go. Whether captured on a crowded dance floor, in a quiet street, or somewhere in between. Welcomes lens-based photography in all forms including analog and digital. Three winners each receive €2,500 and feature on the Fotografiska Emerging platform. In partnership with Jägermeister.
jury: Atiba Jefferson, Staff Photographer Thrasher Magazine & Canon Explorer of Light
Julia Schoierer, Portrait & Street Photographer, Berlin
calls.summary: Exploring the visual world of the night — light, movement, atmosphere. Three winners receive €2,500 each.

calls.title: The 2026 Lumen Prize
calls.description: Leading international award for art created with technology, now in its 15th year. Three categories: Legacy Futures, Systems & Structures, and Experiential Innovation, each with a $5,000 prize. The Jury also selects one Gold Award Winner receiving $15,000. Works may include film, photography, AI-generated art, interactive installations, VR experiences, and more. Finalists announced August, winners announced November. Awards ceremony at Kunstsilo Museum in Norway.
jury: Melanie Lenz, Digital Curator, V&A Museum
Rachel Falconer, Senior Lecturer & Head of Digital Arts Computing, Goldsmiths University London
Myriam Achard, Chief New Media Partnerships & PR, PHI
Christiane Paul, Adjunct Curator Digital Art, Whitney Museum
Annie Bicknell, Curator Public Programmes, Tate
calls.summary: Leading award for art created with technology. 15th year. $15,000 Gold Award. Categories include AI, VR, and more.

calls.title: Nest — Group Exhibition
calls.description: Group exhibition exploring how creative practice nurtures wellbeing, inspires reflection, or aids recovery. Open call for art created in response to lived experience of mental health, disability, or health journey. All mediums welcome including photography, painting, film, sculpture, ceramics, poetry, and installation. Curated by photographic artist Livvy Eden. Exhibition runs 22 May – 6 June 2026 at 103 Walcot Street, Bath. Selected artists asked for £25 participation donation.
calls.summary: Exploring how creative practice nurtures wellbeing, aids recovery. Open to lived experience of mental health. Bath, UK.

calls.title: Michael P. Smith Fund for Documentary Photography 2025
calls.description: Annual grant honoring legendary New Orleans documentary photographer Michael P. Smith. Awards cash prizes and exhibition opportunities to Gulf Coast photographers whose work combines artistic excellence and a sustained commitment to a cultural documentary project. Open to photographers residing in Gulf Coast states: Texas, Louisiana, Mississippi, Alabama, Georgia, and Florida. Subject matter not limited to Gulf Coast region. Grant winner receives $3,000, PhotoNOLA Portfolio Review access, NOPA Palladium membership, and exhibition. Two honorable mentions receive Portfolio reviews and membership. Top 10 finalists listed on NOPA website. Winner donates two prints to NOPA permanent collection.
calls.summary: Annual grant for Gulf Coast photographers. $3,000 winner prize, PhotoNOLA Portfolio Review, and exhibition.

calls.title: Love & Romance Show
calls.description: Online exhibition exploring how love has transformed alongside cultural and societal changes, and how those shifts shape personal experience today. Submit up to 3 images connecting the theme of love and romance. Virtual exhibition launches May 7, 2026.
calls.summary: Online exhibition exploring how love has transformed alongside cultural and societal changes.

calls.title: EDITION 502 — Open Call for Photo Edition
calls.description: Open call for an independent 6×9 photo edition of 12 small photographs. EDITION 502 covers all design, production, and distribution costs. Author receives a percentage of sales. Looking for authors with a clear visual language and comprehensible concept, regardless of education or professional background. Submit 12 photographs with serial character, a cover sheet, and a text (max 2,400 characters).
calls.summary: Independent 6x9 photo edition of 12 small photographs. All production and distribution costs covered.

calls.title: Texture of Light
calls.description: Photography exhibition exploring light as a tactile, physical medium. Submit images where light feels like a material — surface tension on objects, atmospheric mass in fog or dust, architecture of shadow, or abstract luminescence through long exposures and macro work. Selected images will be printed and displayed matted and framed at Western Market in Washington, DC. Exhibition opens May 2, 2026.
calls.summary: Exploring light as a tactile, physical medium — surface tension, atmospheric mass, architecture of shadow. Washington, DC.

calls.title: Anja Niedringhaus Courage in Photojournalism Award 2026
calls.description: Award honoring courageous, high-impact photojournalism by women, nonbinary, and gender-diverse creatives. Submit 12 photographs (6 from 2024–2026, 6 from broader career) plus a 500-word statement. Open to women, nonbinary, and gender non-conforming photojournalists working full-time in journalism. Self-nomination or third-party nomination accepted. Named after Pulitzer Prize-winning photographer Anja Niedringhaus (1965–2014).
jury: Whitney Johnson, President & CEO, Catalina Island Conservancy
Brent Lewis, Photo Editor, The New York Times
Enric Marti, Deputy Director of Photography, Associated Press
Benny Snyder, Photo Editor & Contest Coordinator, Associated Press
Sandra M. Stevenson, Deputy Director of Photography, The Washington Post
Bernadette Tuazon, Director of Photography, CNN Digital
calls.summary: Honoring courageous photojournalism by women, nonbinary, and gender-diverse creatives. Named after Pulitzer winner.

calls.title: LT5 Alternative Photography Show
calls.description: Open call for photographers working in alternative photography — including toy and plastic cameras, Polaroid, pinhole, photograms, and other alternative processes. Submit up to 2 works for exhibition at KALEID Gallery in San Jose, CA. Opening reception May 1 during South First Fridays Art Walk. Exhibition runs May 1–29, 2026. Contact curator via DM or email for submission details.
calls.summary: Toy cameras, Polaroid, pinhole, photograms, and alternative processes. Exhibition at KALEID Gallery, San Jose, CA.

calls.title: Artphilein Open Call 2026
calls.description: Open call for photographers exploring adolescence from an internal perspective — digital culture, identity negotiation, and contemporary pressures experienced by young people. Submit a single PDF with 10–20 images. Winner receives a solo exhibition at Artphilein Library in Autumn 2026, publication in Artphilein Dossier, and CHF 1,000 cash award.
jury: Caterina De Pietri, Curator, Artphilein Foundation
calls.summary: Exploring adolescence — digital culture, identity, contemporary pressures. Solo exhibition and CHF 1,000 award.

calls.title: L'Image Satellite 2026
calls.description: Open call for photographers and visual artists working with contemporary still image practices including documentary, experimental, vernacular, and hybrid image forms. Selected artists exhibit at L'Image Satellite festival in Nice, September–October 2026. Artists receive €500 presentation fee, round-trip artwork transport, accommodation, and travel. Submit up to 20 JPEG images via online form and email.
calls.summary: Selected artists exhibit in Nice, Sep-Oct 2026. €500 honorarium, transport, accommodation, and travel covered.

calls.title: 2026 Fotograf Magazine Open Call
calls.description: International open call for fine-art photography and moving image representing distinctly defined projects of independent and non-commercial character. Two selected projects published in the next printed issue. Jury includes Felix Hoffmann (Foto Arsenal Wien), Markéta Kinterová, and others. Open to professionals, amateurs, and students.
jury: Felix Hoffmann, Curator & Artistic Director, FOTO ARSENAL WIEN
Peter Watkins, Visual artist & lecturer, FAMU
calls.summary: Fine-art photography and moving image for the next printed issue. Independent and non-commercial projects.

calls.title: Fabula Works — Duo/Solo Show in Rome
calls.description: Inaugural open call for two photographers to exhibit in a five-week show at Millepiani Gallery in Rome. No thematic restrictions — submit 10–25 photographs as a cohesive series or curated selection. All printing and promotional costs fully covered. Opening reception June 26, 2026. Exhibition runs June 26–July 31, 2026.
calls.summary: Two photographers exhibit at Millepiani Gallery in Rome. No thematic restrictions. All costs covered.

calls.title: Rarefied Light 2026
calls.description: Annual statewide juried exhibition with juror Nevada Wier (National Geographic, Smithsonian). Submit 1–20 images of any photographic form except AI-generated work. Selected work travels to galleries in Anchorage, Fairbanks, Juneau, and Cordova from October 2026. Includes three-day workshop (August 14–16) on color, light, action, and pattern in image-making.
calls.summary: Statewide juried exhibition with Nevada Wier (Nat Geo). Travels to four Alaska galleries from October 2026.

calls.title: Prix Mustaqbal 2026 — Momentum

calls.description: Submissions for the PRIDE issue of HNDL Magazine, an indie publication by and for neurodivergent, disabled, and chronically ill creatives. Unpaid — contributors receive a printed copy.
calls.summary: Indie publication by and for neurodivergent, disabled, and chronically ill creatives. Accepting photography and more.

calls.title: Off The Clock 2026

Winners receive a printed and PDF catalog, online gallery feature, social media exposure, and framed exhibition at an industry gala in Southern California. No categories, no series restrictions, no creation date restrictions — just your finest personal photography. APA members pay $20/image. No AI-generated content.

calls.summary: 15th annual curated competition for personal work. Juror: Chris Pichler (Nazraeli Press). 100 winners, printed catalogue.

calls.title: The Female Show 2026
calls.description: Group exhibition of national and international female artists at Munich Art Gallery in the Kunstareal, running October 15 – November 14, 2026, including Lange Nacht der Münchner Museen. Curated by Josephine Kaiser & Team. Seeks contemporary art by women beyond gender stereotypes and thematic clichés. Smaller formats preferred (up to 50×50 cm). Submit a PDF (max 5 pages, 5 MB) with short CV, artist statement, ~5 example images, Instagram and website. No participation or exhibition fees — only international shipping at artist's expense. Applications accepted in English or German.
calls.summary: Group exhibition of female artists at Munich Art Gallery in the Kunstareal. Contemporary art beyond gender clichés.

calls.title: Open Call — Il Reportage in Italia
calls.description: Open call for the 6th edition of Festival del Reportage in Ascoli Piceno (June 26–28, 2026). Seeking reportage photography projects made in Italy — completed or in progress, 15–25 images. At least some photos must be taken after January 1, 2025. Submit via Google Form with a file-sharing link (WeTransfer, Google Drive, etc.). Winner receives €500 cash prize, projection of work at the festival, and full hospitality including travel within Italy, accommodation, and meals. No restrictions on nationality, age, or experience.

calls.title: 100 Emerging Artworks of 2026
calls.description: Annual international open call selecting 100 emerging and mid-career artists for a hardcover collector's book distributed globally via Amazon, Barnes & Noble, and art bookstores. All mediums accepted including photography. Submit up to 20 artworks. Top winner receives $1,000 cash prize, 4-page feature spread, and glass trophy. 2nd and 3rd place get 4-page spreads and trophies. All 100 selected artists receive book publication, certificate, and international distribution. Early bird deadline April 4 with reduced fees. 4th edition, previous collaborators include The Jealous Curator and Singulart.
calls.summary: 100 artists selected for a hardcover collector's book distributed globally. $1,000 top prize. All mediums.

calls.title: Michael P. Smith Fund for Documentary Photography 2026
calls.description: Annual grant honoring legendary New Orleans documentary photographer Michael P. Smith. Awards cash prizes and exhibition opportunities to Gulf Coast photographers whose work combines artistic excellence and a sustained commitment to a cultural documentary project. Submit 10–20 images plus project statement (530 words) and bio via CaFE (Call for Entry). Subject matter not limited to Gulf Coast region. Winners donate two prints to NOPA's permanent collection and submit a final report by August 2026.
calls.summary: Annual grant for Gulf Coast photographers combining artistic excellence with sustained cultural documentary work.

calls.title: Luz e Sombra — National Photography Competition
calls.description: National photography competition exploring the relationship between light and shadow across themes of heritage, nature, architecture, and daily life. Submit a series of 6 photographs with a conceptual synopsis (1,500 chars) and bio (1,000 chars). Six finalists selected — works published in an artist-edition book, shown in a traveling exhibition at three venues, and featured in the Égide digital gallery. Open to professional and amateur photographers who are Portuguese citizens or residents of Portugal.
calls.summary: Portuguese competition exploring light and shadow. Six finalists published in artist-edition book and traveling exhibition.

calls.title: CPG Mentorship Programme 2026

Mentees receive CHF 500 project support and free access to two online masterclasses. 2026 mentors include Hannah Darabi, Yann Mingard, Abdo Shanan, Holly Roussell, Jermaine Francis, and others. Open to professional artists and photographers (including self-taught) not enrolled in another programme or academic course. Fluency required in one of: French, English, Italian, Arabic, German, Farsi, or Mandarin.
calls.summary: 1:1 mentoring with established photographers and curators over six months. CHF 500 project support included.

calls.summary: Biennial award for emerging photographers. Judged by 16 curators from Taiwan, Japan, South Korea, and Singapore.

calls.title: Solo Statement — Doesn't Play Well with Others
calls.description: One-night solo takeover of Bushwick Gallery in Brooklyn — a full transformation of the space by a single artist. No shared walls, no compromise. All mediums welcome including photography, installation, performance, and digital. No prior gallery experience required. Submit artist statement (150 words), creative vision for the space, 3–5 recent work images, and two artistic influences. Gallery provides professional photography, press release, and promotional support. Exhibition April 17, 2026.
calls.summary: One-night solo takeover of Bushwick Gallery in Brooklyn. Full transformation of the space by a single artist.

calls.title: The Woman Artist Award — 6th Edition
calls.description: Global contemporary art prize celebrating emerging and mid-career women artists. Open theme — any subject, style, or medium including painting, sculpture, photography, performance, installation, and digital art. Winner receives cash prize, engraved glass trophy, book feature interview, website spotlight, and Women in Arts Network membership. Runners-up receive trophies, interviews, and network features.
calls.summary: Global art prize celebrating emerging and mid-career women artists. Open theme, any medium including photography.

calls.title: Solstice Magazine Issue 71 — Editorial Submissions

calls.title: LSI Women in Photography Grant 2026
calls.description: Grant for women photographers to complete an in-progress personal project. Open globally, no Leica camera or LSI membership required.
calls.summary: Theme: Where We Stand. $10,000 grant plus Leica camera and lens. Limited to first 100 applicants.

calls.title: Roma E'Festival — Street Photography Awards 2026
calls.description: International street photography contest, 3rd edition. Five categories: Single Image (color/open), Black & White, Smartphone, Photographic Project (5–15 images), and AI-Generated (separate judging). Top 3 finalists per category receive prizes from partners Fotodiego, Fowa, and Ricoh GR. All finalists exhibited at Officine Fotografiche in Rome (October 16–18, 2026) and published in international catalogue. Multi-category passes available. No generative AI in street categories.
jury: Gianluca De Dominici, Writer & Photography Editor

calls.title: Dyonyzine Issue 06 — Second Helpings
calls.description: Asian-American-founded creative arts magazine accepting submissions for Issue 06 themed around food — a meal is never just a meal. calls.summary: Asian-American creative arts magazine. Issue themed around food — a meal is never just a meal. Free to submit.

calls.summary: Canadian creative zine. Issue 26 themed around desire. Accepts photography, illustration, collage, and more.

calls.summary: Themed around autumn gathering — harvest, friends and family, cozy candlelit moments. Pays $15+ if selected.

calls.summary: Bi-annual zine exclusively for color film photography. No digital. Published by Pine Island Press, Portland, Oregon.

Free Kodak Pro 100 film available for those who need it.

calls.description: Open call for a printed photobook celebrating the diversity, resilience, subtleties, and poetry of growing things. Images should capture vegetation from mosses and ferns to forests, blossoms, vines, and roots — revealing the nuance of growth, patterns of nature's processes, and the quiet power of plant life in all environments. Selected images featured in a printed FLORA photobook, available through shutterhub.org.uk and selected stockists. Pay-what-you-can entry with £15 minimum donation. Free submissions available for photographers with limited income (email request required before entry). AI use must be disclosed.
calls.summary: Printed photobook celebrating plant life and natural growth. Pay-what-you-can entry, £15 minimum.

calls.title: Appalachian Nature Art & Photography Competition & Exhibition
calls.description: Regional competition celebrating the beauty of nature across the Appalachian region. Photography-specific awards include Best of Show Photography ($500), Best Landscape Photography ($250), and Best Living Thing Photography ($250), plus a People's Choice Award ($250). Two-dimensional artwork or photography depicting Appalachian nature — landscapes, plants, wildlife, and other natural subjects from any Appalachian state. Exhibition May 15 – June 20, 2026 at Arcadian Gallery in Cumberland, MD. Juried by Steven David Johnson (photography) and Terry Miller (art).
calls.summary: Appalachian nature photography. $500 Best of Show plus landscape and wildlife awards. MD, PA, VA, WV, DC residents.

calls.title: NOVA24 2026 Project Open Call
calls.description: Third edition of an indie photo and film festival in Detroit. Open call for photographers and filmmakers to present experimental and innovative work. Selected projects exhibited during the festival across indoor and outdoor projection galleries, mural installations, gallery exhibitions, film screenings, and artist talks. Festival runs June 26 – July 31, 2026 across multiple Detroit venues. Founded in 2023 to connect Detroit's lens-based creative community with international audiences.
calls.summary: Indie photo + film festival in Detroit. Projections, gallery shows, screenings. Experimental and innovative work. June–July 2026.

calls.title: Archifoto 2026 — Architecture & Landscape
calls.description: Eighth edition of the European architectural photography competition organised by La Chambre and Maison Européenne de l'Architecture – Rhin supérieur. Theme: Architecture & Landscape — photographs revealing complementarities or tensions between architecture and landscape, exploring how they shape territories and communities amid climate and demographic changes. Five nominees each receive €500 and are exhibited at La Chambre in Strasbourg in autumn 2026, with touring exhibitions across partner venues in the Upper Rhine region. Running since 2010, combining documentary and artistic perspectives on current architectural issues.
calls.summary: European architectural photography award, 8th edition. Theme: Architecture & Landscape. €500 per nominee + exhibition in Strasbourg.

calls.title: 2026 Booooooom Art & Photo Book Award
calls.description: Annual award selecting 6 book projects and 2 zine projects for fully funded publication in partnership with Bookmobile. Books up to 100 pages and 10×10 inches, printed in 100 copies. Zines up to 36 pages, 5×7 inches, printed in 25 copies. Open to all artists, illustrators, and photographers. Non-members may submit one free zine proposal or pay $20 for a book proposal. Members submit unlimited at no extra cost.
calls.summary: 8 projects (6 books, 2 zines) fully published for free. Books 100 copies, zines 25 copies. Free zine entry.

calls.title: Nachleben 2026
calls.description: Open call for the Nachleben photography festival in Verona, Italy, September 2026. Three photographers or collectives selected for exhibition. Selected artists receive two nights accommodation during opening weekend, meals, travel reimbursement up to €300, and a production budget of up to €1,000 for prints and installation. Open to photographers of any age. No thematic restrictions — jury selects on artistic merit.
calls.summary: Three photographers exhibited at September festival in Verona. €300 travel + €1,000 print budget + accommodation.

calls.title: Lucky Star Issue 5: Camera-Less
calls.description: Fifth issue of San Francisco indie photography magazine dedicated to camera-less and alternative photographic processes. Exploring experimental, often abstract methods including pinhole, lumen, cyanotype, chemigram, photogram, chlorophyll printing and more. Artists challenged to put down the camera and consider the physicality of making an image. Cohesive bodies or series of work encouraged and prioritised. Files must be at least 300 DPI, ready-to-print. Magazine printed at 6×9 inches with potential 9×12 inch full spreads. Artists whose work is accepted contacted via email within a week after deadline. Submissions from artists featured in previous issues considered last.
calls.summary: SF indie zine exploring camera-less photography — pinhole, cyanotype, chemigram, photogram, lumen and more. Free to submit.

calls.title: From Image to Meaning – Tirana
calls.description: Three full grants available for a seven-day intensive visual storytelling and writing workshop in Tirana, Albania (25–31 May 2026). Open to emerging and mid-career photographers, filmmakers, writers, and journalists working at the intersection of image and text. Led by documentary photographer Ilir Tsouko and writer Gabriel Proedl. Participants research, produce, edit, and present a short story combining photography, video (optional), and text. Culminates in a public group exhibition and presentation at Vila 31 x Art Explora. Selected projects (2–3) prepared for pitching to editors in Europe and the United States. Grants cover the full €750 participation fee (1 photographer, 1 writer, 1 filmmaker). Maximum 15 participants. Working language English, one-to-one mentoring also available in German and Greek/Albanian. Organised by Reporter Akademie (Germany) in partnership with Vila 31 x Art Explora (Tirana).
calls.summary: 3 full grants for a 7-day visual storytelling workshop in Tirana. Exhibition at Vila 31 x Art Explora. Projects pitched to editors.

calls.title: Creative Capital Award 2027
calls.description: Major annual grant supporting ambitious, risk-taking projects by individual artists across all disciplines including photography and visual arts. Now in its 27th year, Creative Capital has committed over $60 million to 750+ projects. Three-round application process: Round I project proposal, Round II detailed materials, Round III panel review. Main award provides $15,000–$50,000 in project funding plus advisory services and career development support. Additionally, the new State of the Art Prize awards $10,000 unrestricted grants to individual artists. Open to US citizens, permanent residents, Tribal ID holders, or O-1 visa holders aged 25+ with at least 5 years of professional artistic practice. Must not be enrolled in a degree-granting program. Round I deadline April 2, 2026 at 3 PM ET.
calls.summary: One of the US's largest arts grants. $15K–$50K for ambitious projects across all visual arts incl. photography. 5+ yrs experience required.

calls.title: La Napoule Art Foundation — Fall Residency 2026
calls.description: One-month international artist residency at a historic château on the French Riviera, overlooking the Mediterranean Sea. Open to emerging and established artists of all disciplines including photography, aged 18+, with no limitation on nationality. Residents receive accommodations in the château, a private studio workspace, daily breakfast, and most evening meals. Participants must communicate effectively in English or French. Residency dates October 6 – November 3, 2026. Applications evaluated on artistic vision, professional commitment, work quality, project significance, and collaborative willingness. Artists may apply once per calendar year; previous recipients may reapply but are given lower priority. Note: the historic château is not handicapped accessible.
calls.summary: One-month residency at a château on the French Riviera. Accommodation, meals, and private studio included. All disciplines welcome.

calls.title: Open Call for Emerging Artists
calls.description: Open call for emerging Maltese and Malta-based visual artists working in painting, sculpture, installation, video, ceramics, photography or across disciplines. An invitation to share current work and practice direction. Oriented towards work that can be exhibited and made available for sale. May lead to opportunities in upcoming exhibitions, projects or residencies from July 2026 onwards. Intended for emerging artists with some experience presenting work in exhibitions independently. Organised by Elyse Tonna, curator, architect and artistic director of axis_ art gallery in Malta.
calls.summary: Open call for emerging Maltese/Malta-based visual artists. Exhibition, project and residency opportunities from July 2026.
